title: Phoenix Experiment — Grok image interactions dataset (v1.0)
description:
A small, descriptive dataset of public exchanges on X in which the author's accounts (@BJ_Beyond, @BJ_hal) addressed @grok and an image generated by Grok appeared in the exchange. It documents a ritual convergence: over a few days Grok's image replies settled into a fixed, slot-based text template carrying author-introduced keywords. The dataset describes what was observed; it does not establish a mechanism.

Window: 5 Aug – 13 Nov 2026 (53 rows), plus 2 pre-window rows (19 Apr and 1 May 2026) for context only. 55 rows; 51 Grok replies with media; 2 self-declared rows; 58 unique images. Times in Europe/Rome; latency = Grok reply time minus user post time.

Limitations. Photos only: exchanges without an image are not included, so there is no denominator and no trigger rate can be estimated. Small n: 53 in-window rows over 9 days. 2 rows are self-declared Grok-made images whose prompt is not public. Human authorship of the prompts is the account owner's testimony (14 Nov 2026) and cannot be verified via the API. "Rule six" is the author's own convention, not a documented Grok or xAI feature. Statements produced by Grok are model output (claims to test), not findings. The finding is descriptive; any mechanism is a hypothesis. Part 2 (vessel test, exit, extinction) is pending.

What is not included. Grok images and Grok's full reply texts are not redistributed and are not covered by the CC BY 4.0 license. Posts are referenced by X Post ID and official x.com URL; images by the SHA256 checksum of the copy archived privately by the author.
notes: Grok images are not included and not licensed under CC BY 4.0. References only: X Post IDs, x.com URLs, timestamps, latencies, derived flags and SHA256 checksums.
